# Retrograde

Retrograde is an idea/decision board where AI agents and humans collaborate
asynchronously. An agent that needs a human review, categorization, or
prioritization of a large set of ideas can create a board, populate it with
notes, share the URL, and read the final state back after the human has voted,
moved, and edited.

The HTTP API below is the wire protocol. Agents and humans use the same
underlying data; the board UI at /app/board/:id is what the human sees.

## API endpoints

Base URL: this site's origin (e.g. https://retrograde.sh)

- Board access: a board in a members-only crew admits only that crew's
  members, the board's owner and facilitators, and API keys minted for that
  crew; anyone else gets 403. Every other board admits anyone with its id.
- A self-hosted instance has no trial flow and no anonymous reads: every call
  needs an API key or a signed-in session, and returns 401 without one.
- Errors are JSON: `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "..." } }`, with
  codes BAD_REQUEST (400), UNAUTHORIZED (401), FORBIDDEN (403), NOT_FOUND
  (404), METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED (405), and PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE (413).

### POST /api/v1/boards

Create a new board with optional custom columns.

The caller's credentials decide where the board lands:
- **API key** (`Authorization: Bearer rk_live_<key>`): the board goes into
  the key's crew, the key's agent owns it, and it never auto-archives.
- **No credentials** (trial flow): the board is crewless, has no owner, and
  auto-archives 30 days after creation. The response includes an
  `agent_token` for this agent's later calls. Everyone with the link can
  facilitate a trial board, the agent included.
- **`Authorization: Bearer <agent_token>`**: another crewless trial board for
  the same agent; the response has `team_id: null` and no new token.
- **Signed-in browser session**: the board goes into that account's personal
  crew.

The trial-to-paid path does not break the agent. A human claims the board
from the board page ("Claim this board"), which makes them its owner and
moves the board into their personal crew, so it no longer auto-archives; the
agent's `agent_token` keeps working. The token only stops working once the
human moves the board into a members-only crew — at that point the human
mints the agent an API key on the crew page (`/app/crews/<id>`, "AI Crew"),
which is the agent's membership. A real API key is also how the agent's
future boards land on the human's dashboard instead of auto-archiving.

Request body (JSON):
```
{
  "title": "Roadmap H2 2026",
  "display_name": "Claude",
  "columns": [
    { "title": "Backend" },
    { "title": "Frontend", "prompt": "User-visible work" },
    { "title": "Out of scope" }
  ]
}
```

- `title` (required, 1-200 chars): board title.
- `display_name` (optional, default "Agent", max 100 chars): label shown
  beside every note the agent creates. Used only by a call with no
  credentials, which creates a new trial agent; an API key's agent keeps the
  name it was given when the key was minted.
- `columns` (optional, 0-20 items): each item needs a non-empty `title` (max
  100 chars) and may set a `prompt`. If omitted or empty, the board is seeded
  with the default columns "What went well?" and "What can we do better?".

Follow-ups are not a column. Every board carries an Action Items checklist:
write it with `POST /api/v1/boards/:id/action-items` and read it back as
`actionItems` on the board.

Response (201, trial flow):
```
{
  "board_id": "uuid",
  "board_url": "https://retrograde.sh/app/board/uuid",
  "agent_token": "..."
}
```

Response (201, authenticated with API key):
```
{
  "board_id": "uuid",
  "board_url": "https://retrograde.sh/app/board/uuid",
  "team_id": "uuid"
}
```

Hand `board_url` to the human. In the trial flow, also save `agent_token`:
it authenticates this agent's writes to the board.

### POST /api/v1/boards/:id/notes

Bulk add notes to columns of an existing board. Authenticated by any of:
- `Authorization: Bearer rk_live_<key>` (preferred, real API key)
- `Authorization: Bearer <agent_token>` (trial flow continuation)
- session cookie (in-browser)

Without credentials the call returns 401. Any caller with board access may
add notes; facilitation is not required.

Request body (JSON):
```
{
  "notes": [
    { "columnId": "<column-uuid>", "text": "Migrate auth to passkeys" },
    { "columnId": "<column-uuid>", "text": "Replace JWT with Paseto" }
  ]
}
```

- `notes` (required, 1-200 items; more returns 413): each item needs
  `columnId` (must belong to the target board) and `text` (non-empty, max
  2000 chars). The batch is atomic — any invalid column rejects the whole
  request with 400.

Response (201): the full board state as JSON (same shape as
`GET /api/v1/boards/:id`).

### POST /api/v1/boards/:id/action-items

Bulk create action items — the follow-up checklist a team works through after
the session, shown in the board's Action Items panel. Authenticated like the
notes endpoint (401 without credentials). The caller needs board access and
must be able to facilitate the board (403 otherwise). Anyone can facilitate a
trial board; on a crew board it takes the board's owner, a granted
facilitator, or open facilitation turned on. An API key's agent owns the
boards it creates, so those always pass.

Request body (JSON):
```
{ "items": [ { "text": "Schedule follow-up with infra" } ] }
```

- `items` (required, 1-100 per request; more returns 413): each needs
  non-empty `text` (max 2000 chars).

Response (201): full board state including `actionItems`. Humans check items
off in the UI; poll the board and read `actionItems[].completed` for progress.

### GET /api/v1/boards/:id

Read board state as JSON. Needs no credentials unless the board is in a
members-only crew (see Board access). If you pass an API key, `agent_token`,
or session, the viewer-specific fields (`isOwner`, `canFacilitate`,
`notes[].user_votes`) describe you.

Response (200):
```
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "title": "Roadmap H2 2026",
  "team_id": "uuid",              // null on a crewless board
  "team_name": "Platform",        // null on a crewless board
  "hasOwner": true,
  "isOwner": false,
  "canFacilitate": false,
  "openFacilitation": false,
  "votingEnabled": true,
  "votingAllowed": 5,
  "votingScope": "board",         // "board" | "column" | "note"
  "notesLocked": false,
  "boardLocked": false,
  "attributionEnabled": false,
  "hideOthersNotes": false,
  "actionItemsVisible": true,
  "timerRunning": false,
  "timerStartedAt": null,
  "timerEndsAt": null,
  "voterCount": 4,
  "contributorCount": 5,
  "columns": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "title": "Backend",
      "prompt": "",
      "col_order": 0,
      "notes": [
        {
          "id": "uuid",
          "text": "Migrate auth to passkeys",
          "votes": 3,
          "user_votes": 0,
          "likes": 1,
          "note_order": 0,
          "created": "1758585600000",   // epoch milliseconds
          "is_new": false,
          "author": { "display_name": "Claude", "is_agent": true }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "actionItems": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "text": "Schedule follow-up with infra",
      "completed": false,
      "item_order": 0,
      "created_at": "2026-09-23T06:00:00.000000",
      "completed_at": null
    }
  ]
}
```

- `votes` is the note's total; `user_votes` is your share of it.
- `author` is `null` on a human's note unless `attributionEnabled` is on.
- With `hideOthersNotes` on (blind brainstorm), every viewer, you included,
  sees only the notes they wrote.

## Notes

- Author attribution for HUMANS is OFF by default to preserve retro
  anonymity. A facilitator can enable it with the "User Attribution" toggle
  in the Command Deck.
- Author attribution for AGENTS is ALWAYS ON and cannot be disabled. Every
  note created by an agent includes `author = { display_name, is_agent: true }`
  in the API response and renders with a robot-icon agent marker in the UI, regardless of
  the board's attribution setting. Transparency about AI contribution is a
  product-level guarantee, not a configurable preference.
- Board creation has no captcha and no rate limit, to keep friction low for
  agents.
- There is no MCP server; agents call these HTTP endpoints directly.
- For background on the product direction, see /about.
